properties.title: Mg# Magnesium Number · Kaguya MI 65N-65S (Shi et al. 2026)
properties.authors: Shi X., Chen J., Wang J., Liu S., Tong X., Li J., Yan Z., Wen S., Xie H., He Z., Chu J., Hu W., Wang F.
properties.producer_institution_name: Tongji University; Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
properties.crs: Source: 9 GeoTIFFs of 20480 x 66560 px, geographic GCS_Moon_2000 in degrees on the 1737400 m sphere. COG: the 9 joined, IAU:30100, same sphere and grid.
properties.processing:lineage: Kaguya Multiband Imager level 5 reflectance after terrain shadow correction (8 bands, 415 to 1550 nm) and the spectral angles θTi and θFe, inverted with a residual 1D CNN (Res-CNN). Leave-one-out training on 56 samples from Apollo, Luna, Chang'E-5, and Chang'e-6 sites gives 56 models whose weights are averaged. The authors compute Mg# from the resulting MgO and FeO maps: Mg# = 100 x (MgO/40.304) / (MgO/40.304 + FeO/71.844), matching the published values within 0.03. Distributed as 9 Float32 GeoTIFFs of 40° longitude, 65N to 65S, 512 ppd, values 0 to 100; batches 2 and 3 appear twice on Figshare with identical content. COG: gdalbuildvrt joins the 9 files (one grid, no resampling); gdal_calc.py maps the source NoData (3.4e38) to -9999 and sets -9999 where the MgO map is NoData; gdal_translate assigns IAU:30100 and writes a COG with DEFLATE/PREDICTOR=3 compression.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Mg# (molar Mg/(Mg+Fe)) indicates magma differentiation: high Mg# marks primitive, Mg-rich material and low Mg# evolved, iron-rich mare basalt. 59 m/pixel between 65N and 65S.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Mg# computed from Res-CNN MgO and FeO (Kaguya MI, Chang'e-6 calibrated), 59 m/pixel, 65N-65S. RMSE 1.08 at the training sites. NoData where MgO is NoData.
properties.lri:quality_note: RMSE 1.08 between map and measured Mg# at the 56 training sites. The COG sets Mg# to NoData where MgO is NoData (0.566% of valid source pixels): there the published Mg# rests on MgO values outside 1 to 12 wt%, which the MgO map rejects, and 14% of those values fall outside 35 to 80 in sampled windows, against 0.9% elsewhere. The source spans 0 to 100 and is not clipped; 0.168% of valid pixels are below 35 and 0.055% above 80, the range of the article's color bar. Source pixel mean 63.80, equal to the article's global mean (63.8). In the COG, Mg# spans 6.91 to 100, the bounds set by MgO 1 to 12 wt% and FeO 0 to 24 wt%; pixel mean 63.85, NoData 2.32% of pixels. Inherits the clipping of FeO at 0 and 24 wt%: Mg# 100 marks FeO at 0 wt%, mostly artifact patches on slopes poleward of 55°. NoData covers 1.76% of source pixels, mostly in gaps along orbit tracks, and up to 21% of each column within 0.2° west and 0.4° east of 180°. North-south stripes about 1.06° apart, the longitude step between successive Kaguya orbits, appear at 20 to 35°E and 55 to 100°E and more weakly at 110 to 135°W and near 165°E; column means deviate from their 1° running median by up to 3. The source is 9 files of 40° longitude. At 180° the two sides do not match pixel for pixel (mean step -0.58); at 60°E the mean step is +0.18; the other boundaries are continuous. Registered to the LRO frame: at 10 of 12 landing sites the offset to Speyerer et al. (2023) FeO, registered to the LROC WAC mosaic, is within 0.3 km.
